canonical_topic: Power generation technologies: fossil fuel plants
definition: Overview of how fossil fuel power plants generate electricity and their environmental impact.
core_idea: Fossil fuel plants burn oil, natural gas, or coal to create steam that drives a generator; all produce CO2 and other greenhouse gases, with pollution per MWh depending on plant efficiency, and coal is the most polluting fossil fuel by a factor of two to three versus the others.
key_points: Fossil fuel plants burn oil, natural gas, or coal to produce superheated steam that drives a generator
All fossil fuels produce greenhouse gases (e.g., CO2) when burned
More efficient plants use less fuel and thus produce less pollution per megawatt generated
Coal-fired generation is the most polluting fossil fuel, producing two to three times the pollution of oil or natural gas generation
relationships: Heat rate and fossil plants as marginal price setters
trading_implications: Fuel choice and plant efficiency affect a plant's emissions profile, which is relevant to environmental/carbon cost considerations in dispatch economics
